sources.title: Wikipedia: Holy Rosary Seminary
sources.note: Describes the two-storey brick building: rectangular, a symmetrical central block with indented wings, and a ground floor of brick arches. Matched to relation/2418001, the arcaded building facing the Cathedral grounds (Google Street View, July 2015). Its fire and rebuilding dates differ from the NHCP marker's; the marker is followed.

text.en: The seminary began as the Casa de Clérigos, founded by Bishop Andrés González.
Bishop Juan Antonio de Orbigo built a new seminary house in 1785, the Seminario Conciliar de Nueva Cáceres, which Bishop Domingo Collantes inaugurated in 1793.
After a typhoon in 1856 and a fire in 1860, Bishop Francisco Gainza rebuilt and enlarged it in 1862; the Vincentian Fathers took charge in 1865.
Its alumni include Bishop Jorge Barlin, the first Filipino bishop, the propagandist José María Panganiban, and eight of the fifteen Bicol martyrs.
The National Historical Institute declared the seminary a National Historical Landmark under Resolution No. 1 of 1988.
